title: Artin acyclicity for intersections of projective strict localizations
statement:
Let $B$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:P\to B$ be a projective morphism [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Let $x,u$ be any two geometric points of $P$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and form their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$W=P_{(x)}\times_P P_{(u)}.$$
For every torsion abelian sheaf $A$ on the small etale site of $W$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf],
$$H^i(W_{\mathrm{Et}},A)=0\quad\text{for all }i>0,$$
where cohomology is derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The fibre product may be empty or have infinitely many connected components. No Noetherian hypothesis on $B$, constructibility hypothesis on $A$, or invertibility of its torsion orders is imposed.

source.place: Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme, Theorem 7.10 (etale case), Definition 7.8 and Proposition 7.9, printed pp. 14–15; read online, local copy WANTED. Common-affine specialization for projective P: Orgogozo, Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4.

proof.text: Because $p:P\to B$ is projective and $B$ is affine, the projective presentation supplies an affine morphism from $P$ to a relative projective space over $B$. The finite-set affine-neighbourhood lemma [lem-pd-projective-finite-affine-neighbourhood] therefore gives an affine open subscheme $V\subset P$ containing the images of $x$ and $u$. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: Tags 01KP, 01ZY and 00JS; finite-set affine-neighbourhood argument for separated/projective schemes

proof.text: The images of $x$ and $u$ lie in the open $V$, and so do all their generizations, hence the whole images of the canonical maps $P_{(x)}\to P$ and $P_{(u)}\to P$; so both factor through $V$, and $x,u$ are geometric points of $V$. The open immersion $V\hookrightarrow P$ is etale, so ind-etale invariance [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies $V_{(x)}\cong P_{(x)}$ and $V_{(u)}\cong P_{(u)}$ over $P$. Write $P_{(x)}=\operatorname{Spec}B_x$ and $P_{(u)}=\operatorname{Spec}B_u$ with the $R$-algebra structures given by these factorizations through $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$; they are ind-etale $R$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], each of $B_x,B_u$ is a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. A local ring has connected spectrum, so $\operatorname{Spec}B_x$ (resp. $\operatorname{Spec}B_u$) is its own unique connected component and that component is strictly henselian: this is the second, equivalent form of the etale-acyclicity hypothesis of [lem-trf-artin-tensor-etale-acyclic].

source.place: Tags 03Q9, 03PS and 04HX; Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme, Proposition 7.9 (étale case), printed p. 15

proof.text: The fibre product over $P$ equals the fibre product over $V$, since both strict-localization maps factor through the open immersion $V\hookrightarrow P$. Thus $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B_x\otimes_R B_u)$. Apply the Artin tensor-acyclicity node [lem-trf-artin-tensor-etale-acyclic] to obtain vanishing of $H^q(W_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$ for every torsion abelian sheaf $A$ and every $q>0$. This remains valid when the tensor product is zero (so $W$ is empty) or has infinitely many components, because the cited theorem has no finiteness or component-count restriction.

source.place: Theorem 7.10 and Proposition 7.9, pp. 14–15; Stacks Tag 03QO

I split its common-affine specialization: choose an affine neighbourhood of the two points in the projective scheme, identify the two strict localizations with ind-etale strictly henselian algebras over its coordinate ring, apply the Artin tensor-acyclicity theorem, and identify the resulting affine tensor product with the fibre product. The empty and infinitely disconnected cases are retained.
